articles.title: Painting with Gaussians
articles.summary: A new edge-aware pixelation tool has been built to transform images into pixel art by deforming a grid so that it follows image edges instead of naively using a fixed grid over the picture. The same edge information can also be applied in digital painting programs where brush strokes are derived from the image structure and resemble brush marks. This is achieved through the use of Gaussian splats, which map onto the idea of a 2D brush stroke with mean, covariance matrix, color, and opacity encoding its direction and elongation. The tool's interactive feature allows users to test drive Jolt and see how well it works for building non-trivial projects, ultimately determining whether the end result resembles anything like a painting.
